findings.title: Cleanup registers removal of a literal "alias" IDP instead of the created alias
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)`. The string "alias" is a literal, not the IDP alias, so the cleanup attempts to remove an IDP named "alias" that does not exist. The 20 `idp-alias-N` providers created by this test are never removed and leak into the shared test realm, which can change counts in later tests. The same bug appears at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`. The copied pattern in testCacheIDPByOrg (line 303) has the same defect, with an unused `final String alias` variable that was meant to be used.

findings.title: Cleanup for idp-alias-20 uses the literal "alias" and does not remove the IDP
findings.body: The cleanup `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` targets a non-existent IDP named "alias". The IDP `idp-alias-20` created here is never removed, so it leaks into the realm for subsequent tests.

findings.title: remove() now always loads the IDP from the database
findings.body: `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is executed unconditionally. Previously the DB lookup happened only when the alias cache key was invalidated. Every remove now costs an extra DB query, even when the cached entry is available. It is needed for registerIDPLoginInvalidation, but it could reuse the cached IDP for the invalidation of the id and alias keys.

findings.title: Search key includes organizationId even for REALM_ONLY, fragmenting the cache
findings.body: `searchKey` is derived from `organizationId` regardless of `mode`. For REALM_ONLY the result does not depend on organizationId, so callers passing different org ids each produce a separate cached entry (or a cache miss and invalidation via the `cached == null` path) for identical results. The query cache is also rewritten on every such miss, which causes unnecessary churn.
